LESSON: SWIMMING

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS
Strand: Creating and Performing
Topic 2.12.1: Swimming

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Swimming. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How is inverted breaststroke used in life saving?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain the inverted breaststroke and water treading technique in swimming
2. perform water treading skill in swimming
3. perform the inverted breaststroke technique in swimming for skill acquisition

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SWIMMING
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Swimming helps you succeed in CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: SWIMMING
Study Swimming like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain the inverted breaststroke and water treading technique in swimming

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the inverted breaststroke and water treading technique in swimming. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the inverted breaststroke and water treading technique in swimming.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Swimming” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the inverted breaststroke and water treading technique in swimming. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Perform water treading skill in swimming

What this means
In this part you learn to perform water treading skill in swimming. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: perform water treading skill in swimming.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Swimming in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can perform water treading skill in swimming. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Perform the inverted breaststroke technique in swimming for skill acquisition

What this means
In this part you learn to perform the inverted breaststroke technique in swimming for skill acquisition. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: perform the inverted breaststroke technique in swimming for skill acquisition.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can perform the inverted breaststroke technique in swimming for skill acquisition. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Swimming is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Swimming” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: explain the inverted breaststroke and water treading technique in swimming)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Swimming in your own words. (skill: perform water treading skill in swimming)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: perform the inverted breaststroke technique in swimming for skill acquisition)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Swimming to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain the inverted breaststroke and water treading technique in swimming.
3. Practise this skill: perform water treading skill in swimming.
4. Practise this skill: perform the inverted breaststroke technique in swimming for skill acquisition.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Swimming from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Swimming: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Swimming?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How is inverted breaststroke used in life saving?
2. Why is water treading skill important?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Swimming means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain the inverted breaststroke and water treading technique in swimming.
5. Be able to: perform water treading skill in swimming.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
